source.title: Intraday lottery demands in cryptocurrency market
source.author: Manisha Yadav

research_question: Does unusually large recent positive hourly return (lottery demand / MAX) predict lower subsequent 4-hour crypto returns cross-sectionally after realistic costs?
hypothesis: High recent MAX reflects lottery-like demand and temporary overvaluation, so low-MAX assets should outperform high-MAX assets over the next 4 hours.
source_deviation: The paper uses 5-minute returns from the preceding hour and an hourly forecast horizon. Available broad-universe data are 1-hour bars, so this preregistered coarse adaptation uses the maximum hourly close-to-close return over 12/24/48 prior completed hours and a fixed 4-hour holding horizon.
universe_rule: Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals listed by 2021-12-31, including later-delisted contracts where data exist. At each 4-hour decision timestamp retain the top 50 contemporaneously eligible contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.

feature.formula: signal = -max(prior completed hourly close-to-close returns over lookback)
feature.direction: Long lowest-MAX quintile / short highest-MAX quintile.

portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral quintile spread, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: Decision every 4 hours at 00/04/08/12/16/20 UTC; all feature/liquidity inputs end one hour before entry; enter at current 1h bar open and exit at open four hours later.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive low-MAX minus high-MAX spread, canonical net daily-equity Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 lookbacks positive after costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net daily-equity Sharpe >1.0; positive at 2x costs; >=2/3 lookbacks positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; one additional 4-hour execution delay remains positive; DSR reported.
